podcast.body: From the album "Navy Blues," this song is likely Sloan's most recognizable and contributed significantly to that album's strong sales. It is identified as one of Patrick Pentland's "rockers in the key of B" that helped sustain the band's career. "We had a song on it called Money City Maniacs, which is still probably our most recognizable song."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Sloan In Their Own Words: Part 2

podcast.body: This song is presented as an example of the enduring nature of Powerpop. Although recorded in 1998, its style allows it to sound as if it could have been written and recorded any time in the 40 years prior, demonstrating the timeless quality of the genre. "A Powerpop style recorded in 1998. But unless you knew that, it was possible that it might have been written and recorded any time in the last 40 years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
